newsitem.title: USA: Retail buys $63 mln of NYC bonds in presale Monday.
newsitem.headline: Retail buys $63 mln of NYC bonds in presale Monday.

text.p: New York City on Monday said that it had sold $63 million of bonds to individual investors during the second day of a presale order period, making the total so far $133 million.

A New York City official, who declined to be named, added that retail buyers appeared to purchasing bonds further out the yield curve than in previous offerings, in part due to the insurance that the city got for shorter-dated paper.
"We closed out 2011 this morning," the official said, adding the retail interest in getting as much yield as possible was prompting the city to close 2014, 2015 and 2016 maturities as well.
However, it appeared New York City might fall short of the $304 million mark set in an early April bond sale, which while not the record, amounted to over twice the total sold so far.
The present presale order period for individual investors ends on Tuesday at 1300 EDT, and the approximately $740 million offering will be priced for institutional investors on Wednesday.
